selectionRead.selectedClaim: Sozomen describes a council at Milan at which bishops were pressed to condemn Athanasius and dissenting bishops exiled.
selectionRead.sourceCorrection: The raw candidate is the Alexandria 356 raid and must not be narrated as the Milan 355 proceeding.

sources.author: Sozomen (Salamanes Hermeias Sozomenos), Ecclesiastical History IV.9
sources.compositionDate: mid-5th century, commonly c. 440s; exact year not asserted here
sources.exactLocator: Book IV, chapter 9, lines 65-72 in consulted New Advent rendering; especially council, pressure/condemnation and exiles at lines 65-70.
sources.coverageActuallyRead: Read the retrieved chapter-9 passage via page search/open excerpt; not the whole book or Greek text/critical apparatus.
supports: A council convened at Milan; pressure concerning Athanasius' condemnation/exile; Sozomen's account names dissenters and exile.
doesNotSupport: A verbatim transcript, neutral motive attribution, exact hearing room, precise day/month, independently verified attendance figures, or any Alexandrian church raid in 355.
sources.biasAndUncertainty: Fifth-century pro-Nicene church historian, writing long after the event; his language about fear/fraud/ignorance and imperial conspiracy is authorial interpretation. He reports over 300 western bishops, a number independently challenged in Socrates/NPNF editorial notes (possible textual corruption to 30).

sources.coverageActuallyRead: Targeted web find results around §§6 and 24–25 only; not full work/critical edition. URL 2814 is Apologia de Fuga, not Apologia ad Constantium.
supports: Athanasius presents his flight from an Alexandrian nighttime church assault as justified.
sources.biasAndUncertainty: Interested defense by the accused bishop; preserve as his testimony rather than independent corroboration.

selectionRead.sourceTextClaim: Athanasius reports nighttime soldiers entering a church and his escape; Historia Acephala identifies Church of Theonas and Coptic dates 13/14 Mechir.
selectionRead.calendarAssessment: Preserve the source dates Mechir 13/14. Older editions supply parenthetical civil-calendar conversions, which should be attributed to the edition and labeled as conventional Julian/civil conversion; this audit does not certify a proleptic Gregorian date.

sources.kind: primary chronological chronicle; anonymous Alexandrian source transmitted under Athanasius corpus
sources.author: Anonymous compiler of Historia Acephala (annalist); do not automatically equate with the Festal Index sometimes called Chronicon Athanasianum.
sources.compositionDate: late 4th or early 5th century commonly proposed; exact date/authorship unsettled
sources.exactLocator: Section IV.5: Syrianus and Hilary arrive 10 Tybi; night entry into Church of Theonas on 13 Mechir, the night before 14; Athanasius escapes on 14 Mechir. The later church transfer belongs to V.6 (not IV.6); George arrives 30 Mechir per the consulted translation.
sources.coverageActuallyRead: Read the retrieved English page lines 19–22 for IV.5 and the later transfer passage V.6. The translation’s parenthetical date conversions were visible; they are not asserted here as proleptic Gregorian. No critical edition or Coptic manuscript apparatus consulted.
supports: Chronicle's sequence and Coptic date; Church of Theonas; night entry; escape; later separate church transfer and George arrival.
doesNotSupport: By itself, a certain proleptic Gregorian date, exact building footprint, objective troop count, or motive for every actor.
Do not treat Historia Acephala as automatically identical with the Festal Index/Chronicon Athanasianum.
sources.biasAndUncertainty: An anonymous, date-conscious Alexandrian annalist distinct from Athanasius’ own apologetic account; textual gaps/corruption and source relationships require caution. Robertson’s introduction distinguishes the annalist from the Festal Index conventionally called Chronicon Athanasianum; no manuscript/edition identity is assumed.

sources.author: Athanasius of Alexandria, Apologia de Fuga sua
sources.compositionDate: c. 357 CE conventionally assigned; author-date page from Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen academic project describes work as 357
sources.exactLocator: §§24-25 (New Advent displayed lines 128-137); §6 is a separate later sequence and should not be conflated with the initial Syrianus assault.
sources.coverageActuallyRead: Targeted displayed paragraphs §§24-25 via web find, including lines 130-134; not full Greek text or a critical apparatus.
supports: Athanasius says it was night, Syrianus arrived with soldiers, forced entry occurred, he directed congregants to leave, and clergy/monks led him out.
doesNotSupport: A neutral transcript, independently verified figure of more than 5,000 soldiers, exact Coptic date from this passage, exact church identification as Theonas from this passage alone, or dialogue as verbatim historical record.
sources.biasAndUncertainty: First-person polemical self-defense defending flight against accusations of cowardice; the providential framing and troop count are the author's claims.

sources.author: Archibald Robertson, introduction/notes in NPNF series II, vol. IV, Athanasius: Select Works and Letters (1892 edition); modern web host CCEL
sources.publicationDate: 1892 translation/editorial volume; not the date of underlying ancient works
sources.exactLocator: Displayed editorial lines 47-55 and notes 72-73 discuss the interval to George's arrival, common chronological source of Historia Acephala/Festal Index, and why Apologia de Fuga's narrative sequence alone can mislead chronology.
sources.coverageActuallyRead: Read selected commentary/notes only; not the complete volume or modern scholarship reviewing Robertson.
supports: The raid, transfer of churches, and George's later arrival are not to be collapsed into one contiguous event; older chronology debates the relation between narrative order and calendar chronology.
doesNotSupport: A definitive updated calendar conversion independently verified against a modern critical edition.
sources.biasAndUncertainty: Nineteenth-century editorial chronology is useful but dated; its conclusions should not replace current critical edition scholarship.

Do not equate Sulpicius' 'magistri officialibus' with a singular office-holder titled magister officiorum; the text identifies Taurus as praefectus, while later administrative evidence/secondary scholarship specifies praetorian prefect.

sources.kind: primary narrative, later Latin Christian chronicle with eyewitness/hearsay distinctions
sources.author: Sulpicius Severus, Chronica II.41-43
sources.compositionDate: c. 403-404, conventionally; exact composition chronology not fixed to a single day/year
sources.exactLocator: Book II §§41-43; consulted lines 181-189 show §41.1-8 and opening §42. Section 41.1: Taurus is 'praefecto'; §41.2 says 'magistri officialibus' were sent through provinces; §§41.5-8 describe separate church/empty building meeting spaces and delegations.
sources.coverageActuallyRead: Read displayed Latin §§41-42 targeted lines only; English NPNF parallel was surfaced in search results but not used as independent corroboration. Not whole Chronicle/critical apparatus.
supports: Emperor ordered synod at Ariminum; Taurus called praefectus, promised consulship; officials summoned/compelled western bishops, public annona/cellaria; factional split, distinct worship spaces and delegations.
doesNotSupport: Taurus' title as magister officiorum; exact proceedings dates; a single simultaneous session with Seleucia; precise identity/position of the church and vacant hall; reliable neutral headcount.
sources.biasAndUncertainty: Sulpicius writes decades later from a western Nicene perspective; explicitly reports part of his account as what bishop Gavidus used to say and marks his own disagreement (§41.4). Polemical labels and staged spatial contrast are his narrative.

sources.compositionDate: mid-5th century, commonly c. 439; precise date not independently verified here
sources.urlActuallyConsulted: https://www.ccel.org/ccel/s/schaff/npnf202/npnf202.ii.v.xxxvii.html (search/open failed in this pass); available related chapter actually consulted: https://ccel.org/ccel/schaff/npnf202/npnf202.ii.v.xxxvi.html, which is Milan only, not Ariminum.

sources.coverageActuallyRead: II.39 targeted passage read; II.37 consultation failed and remains unconsulted. Do not claim direct consultation of Socrates' Ariminum narrative from this pass.

doesNotSupport: Ariminum procedural details in this pass or the two councils sharing one decision/date/session.

crossEpisodeCautions: Order 23 Milan 355 and order 24 Alexandria 356 are distinct local events. Retain the inherited-source/dispatch distinction; do not use order 24's source passage to substantiate an order 23 hearing.

Order 24 distinguishes the initial Syrianus assault and flight from later 356 church seizures and George's arrival in 357. A Gregorian conversion of the Coptic 13/14 Mechir date needs an edition/calendar note.

Order 25 must preserve Ariminum's western-council process separately from Seleucia's eastern council. Sulpicius says 'Taurus praefectus' and 'magistri officialibus'; later correspondence/prosopography supports 'praetorian prefect'. Avoid 'Magister officiorum' as Taurus' title.
